newsitem.title: USA: U.S. CJD death not linked to beef - Cattlemen.
newsitem.headline: U.S. CJD death not linked to beef - Cattlemen.

text.p: The National Cattlemen's Beef Assn said the Creutzfeldt-Jacob Disease (CJD) that strikes one in a million Americans annually is not the same strain that could be contracted from cattle infected with Bovine Spongiform Encephalophathy (BSE).

"CJD is not new, it is not a public health issue related to beef, and floor traders at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange should not use issues like this to add volatility to the (cattle) market," the NCBA said in a release.

Wire service reports Wednesday that said an Indiana man died from CJD caused panic-like selling that drove cattle prices sharply lower in Chicago cattle futures markets. Traders feared the death could curb beef consumption.
"Since CJD strikes one out of every million Americans each year, this is not an unusual event," the NCBA release said of the latest reported death.
The NCBA said 11 years of surveillance by the U.S. Agriculture Department had yet located Bovine Spongiform Encephalophy (BSE or mad cow disease) in the United States.
Also, it said the Centers for Disease Control has reported no cases of the new variant of CJD in the United States.
